headline: US Special Envoy Sergio Gor to visit Dhaka for 3-day trip
summary: The envoy will meet with PM Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman to discuss strategic relations and visit Rohingya refugees in Cox's Bazar.
details: US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka today for a three-day official visit.
Gor is expected to hold high-level talks with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman on the first day of his visit.
As part of his itinerary, the envoy will travel to Cox's Bazar tomorrow to assess the situation of Rohingya refugees firsthand.
The discussions are expected to focus on Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities, its strategic position in South Asia, and the future of Dhaka-Washington relations.
Washington is also likely to assess Bangladesh's evolving regional role, particularly following recent high-level visits to China, Russia, and Turkey.
If necessary, Gor may convey specific messages from the administration of President Donald Trump to the Bangladeshi leadership.
Gor is the third senior US official to visit Bangladesh since the BNP government took office in February, following visits by Paul Kapur in March and Brendan Lynch in May.
caption:
US Special Envoy Sergio Gor arrives in Dhaka today for a high-stakes three-day visit.

US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka today for a three-day official visit.

Gor is expected to hold high-level talks with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman on the first day of his visit.

As part of his itinerary, the envoy will travel to Cox's Bazar tomorrow to assess the situation of Rohingya refugees firsthand.

The discussions are expected to focus on Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities, its strategic position in South Asia, and the future of Dhaka-Washington relations.

Washington is also likely to assess Bangladesh's evolving regional role, particularly following recent high-level visits to China, Russia, and Turkey.

If necessary, Gor may convey specific messages from the administration of President Donald Trump to the Bangladeshi leadership.

Gor is the third senior US official to visit Bangladesh since the BNP government took office in February, following visits by Paul Kapur in March and Brendan Lynch in May.

headline_marked: India batter [[Ajinkya Rahane retires from international cricket]]
headline: India batter Ajinkya Rahane retires from international cricket
summary: The 38-year-old Mumbai batter, who led India to a historic 2-1 series win in Australia, ends his career with 5,077 Test runs and 12 centuries.
details: Middle-order batter Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from international cricket across all formats on Thursday, ending his pursuit of a recall to the national side.
The Mumbai-born player debuted in T20Is in 2011 and became a mainstay in the Test side, known for his resolute defense and patience in the middle order.
In a social media video, the 38-year-old stated that he feels the timing is right to move on, noting that everything in life has a beginning and an end.
Rahane's career highlight includes leading India to a memorable 2-1 series victory in Australia during 2020-21 as stand-in captain for Virat Kohli.
After India was bowled out for 36 in the Adelaide opener, Rahane's masterful century in Melbourne helped level the series and sparked a remarkable comeback.
As a captain, he remained unbeaten in Test matches, winning four and drawing two of the six tests he led the team in against Australia, Afghanistan, and New Zealand.
Statistically, he finished his international career with 5,077 Test runs at an average of 38.46, including 12 hundreds.
Rahane played his final Test match in July 2023 and had not played white-ball cricket for India since 2018.
He is currently providing commentary for The Hundred in England and will remain active in domestic franchise cricket.
caption:
A historic captain and Test stalwart. Ajinkya Rahane calls time on his international career.

Middle-order batter Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from international cricket across all formats on Thursday, ending his pursuit of a recall to the national side.

The Mumbai-born player debuted in T20Is in 2011 and became a mainstay in the Test side, known for his resolute defense and patience in the middle order.

In a social media video, the 38-year-old stated that he feels the timing is right to move on, noting that everything in life has a beginning and an end.

Rahane's career highlight includes leading India to a memorable 2-1 series victory in Australia during 2020-21 as stand-in captain for Virat Kohli.

After India was bowled out for 36 in the Adelaide opener, Rahane's masterful century in Melbourne helped level the series and sparked a remarkable comeback.

As a captain, he remained unbeaten in Test matches, winning four and drawing two of the six tests he led the team in against Australia, Afghanistan, and New Zealand.

Statistically, he finished his international career with 5,077 Test runs at an average of 38.46, including 12 hundreds.

Rahane played his final Test match in July 2023 and had not played white-ball cricket for India since 2018.

He is currently providing commentary for The Hundred in England and will remain active in domestic franchise cricket.
